To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Ca2+ ions act to depress the end-plate current by reducing the single channel conductance of the ACh-activated end-plate ion channel, without affecting the affinity of ACh for the receptor or the open probability of the channel.

the depressant effects of extracellular Ca2 + on the end- plate channel are not due to the changes in surface charges, the affinity of acetylcholine to the ACh- receptor, or the binding of Ca2 + to intrachannel site, but are probably due to the effect on another binding site of the receptor- channel complex involved in the regulation for ion permeation.
Ca2+ suppresses the end-plate current by reducing the conductance of the acetylcholene receptor-channel complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of calcium (Ca2+) action on the end-plates.
the mechanism by which the end-plate receptor-channel complex regulates its ion conductance and the role of calcium ions in this process.
a study of the mechanism of the calcium action on the ACh receptor-channel complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Ca2+ acts on the ACh receptor-channel complex in the frog end- plate membrane to suppress the increase in the conductance and the number of open channels induced by ACh, without affecting the open time of a single channel.
Ca2+ acts to suppress the ACh-receptive site of the ACh-receptors and the channel opening mechanism of the ACh-channel complex.

the depressant effects of extracellular Ca2+(Ca2+)o on the end- plate channel are not caused by the effects of surface charges, the affinity of ACh, or binding to intracannel sites, but are due to a change of another site involved in regulating ion permeation of ACh-receptor-channel complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ acts at two different sites of the ACh receptor complex: one is the ACh binding site, and the other is the site involved in the gating mechanism.
the depressant action of Ca2+ is mainly due to a decrease in the open probability of the end-plates channel.
the ACh-induced channel is regulated by a Ca2+-sensitive gate in addition to a Ca2+-independent gate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium can act as an inhibitor of the ACh receptor-channel complex.
calcium can affect the function of the ACh receptor in the end-plates of frog muscles.
Ca2+ suppresses the ACh-induced increase in the endplate channel conductance, which may be due to an effect on a site other than the binding sites of Ca2+ and ACh to the receptor-channel complex.
